correctness.rationale: Under equal-sign equal-mass one-dimensional heat particles, conditional integrated covariance of two reflected Gaussian cumulative-field indicators equals −W_r(d)/2 by the half-line covariance identity. Averaging gives V_π=C−μ²/4 Σ_i W_r(a_i−b_π(i)). Directly differentiating the two folded-Gaussian moments gives W_r″ negative for |d|<T_r, positive outside, T_r=σ√(2r(r+1)ln(1+1/r)). The double integral of W_r″ over exchange rectangles gives unique rank optimum when every cross-difference is in the concave region and reverse rank for complete separation beyond T_r. A triangular-kernel second difference has a unique small-δ crossover, second-order offset [(2r+1)ln(1+1/r)−1]δ²/(12T_r); Gaussian tail expansion yields relative gain ratio ∼2 exp(3D²/(4(r+1)σ²)). Independent checks compare 36 exact-enumerated small-dimensional permutations and six curvature signs. Full analytical proof, not finite checks, establishes universality.
